- [Substack: Google Raises $85 Billion and the Market Finally Wakes Up | The Weekly Wrap](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/google-raises-85-billion-and-the) - 2026-06-12

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

The wrap develops Eisman's thesis that AI is shifting funding risk onto public shareholders through equity issuance and higher capital intensity. He contrasts strong Oracle demand with its cash burden and questions model moats and future IPO absorption. He also warns about a 4.5% Treasury threshold, concentrated earnings growth, addiction-related litigation and private-market illiquidity. Primary records support the large financing packages, inflation figures and filed lawsuit while leaving causal market explanations and most forward returns unsettled.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

## Framework and tools

- Compare cash demands with reported earnings and backlog.
- Separate headline aggregate growth from sector concentration.
- Assess illiquidity and benchmark crowding as distinct risks.
- Treat equity issuance and long payoff horizons as investor burdens.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Treasury yield range and index drawdowns.
- Alphabet financing terms, Oracle capex/FCF/RPO and Super Micro proposed issuance.
- Sector earnings-growth expectations.
- Private-equity holding periods and unrealized assets.

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman delivers a solo monologue; inserted advertisements and opening montage are excluded.

- Allegations about addictive design are not adjudicated facts.
